```{r setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results="hide", echo=FALSE}

##set up chunk with necessary packages and data file (.csv) saved on GitHub

library(tidyverse) #needed for pipes etc
library(corrplot) #makes a correlation plot
library(car) #regression diagnostics
library(lmtest) #regression diagnostics 
library(factoextra) #visualization for PCAs

stamer.perio.disease <- read.csv("https://github.com/jstamer95/Al-Qinifab-Oral-Health/blob/main/Stamer%20clean%20data%20all%20no%20missing.csv",
  header = TRUE)
stamer.perio.disease <-data.frame(stamer.perio.disease)
stamer.perio.disease

```

##setting up the summary tables used in the manuscript##########################

```{r}
#Table 1

table_1 <- stamer.perio.disease %>%
  count(time.period) %>%
  mutate(
    percent = round(n / sum(n) * 100),
    time.period = case_when(
      time.period == 4 ~ "Christian Period or Later",
      time.period == 3 ~ "Christian Period",
      time.period == 2 ~ "Post-Meroitic",
      time.period == 1 ~ "Late Meroitic/Post-Meroitic",
      TRUE ~ as.character(time.period)
    )
  )

table_1
```

```{r}
#Table 3

periodontal_groups <- bind_rows(
  
  # Total sample
  stamer.perio.disease %>%
    mutate(
      group_type = "1_Total",
      group = "Total"
    ),
  
  # Sex groups
  stamer.perio.disease %>%
    mutate(
      group_type = "2_Sex",
      group = case_when(
        sex.cat == 1 ~ "Males",
        sex.cat == 2 ~ "Females",
        TRUE ~ "Unknown sex"
      )
    ),
  
  # Time-period groups
  stamer.perio.disease %>%
    mutate(
      group_type = "3_Time period",
      group = case_when(
        time.period == 1 ~ "Late Meroitic/Post-Meroitic",
        time.period == 2 ~ "Post-Meroitic",
        time.period == 3 ~ "Christian Period",
        time.period == 4 ~ "Christian Period or Later",
        TRUE ~ "Unknown time period"
      )
    )
)

periodontal_results <- periodontal_groups %>%
  group_by(group_type, group) %>%
  summarise(
    group_n = n_distinct(Individual),
    
    cej_observed = sum(!is.na(cej.ac)),
    cej_affected = sum(cej.ac >= 2, na.rm = TRUE),
    cej_percent = round(cej_affected / cej_observed * 100),
    mean_cej = mean(cej.ac, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    septum_observed = sum(!is.na(inter.septum)),
    septum_affected = sum(inter.septum >= 3, na.rm = TRUE),
    septum_percent = round(
      septum_affected / septum_observed * 100
    ),
    mean_septum = mean(inter.septum, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  )

table_3 <- periodontal_results %>%
  arrange(group_type, group) %>%
  transmute(
    Group = paste0(group, " (n=", group_n, ")"),
    
    `Percentage with CEJ-AC scores above 2` =
      paste0(
        cej_percent, "% (",
        cej_affected, "/", cej_observed, ")"
      ),
    
    `Average CEJ-AC score` =
      sprintf("%.2f", mean_cej),
    
    `Percentage with interdental septum scores above 3` =
      paste0(
        septum_percent, "% (",
        septum_affected, "/", septum_observed, ")"
      ),
    
    `Average interdental septum score` =
      sprintf("%.2f", mean_septum)
  )

table_3

```

```{r}

#table 4
caries_results <- periodontal_groups %>%
  group_by(group_type, group) %>%
  summarise(
    group_n = n_distinct(Individual),

    caries_observed = sum(!is.na(caries)),

    mean_RC = mean(RC, na.rm = TRUE),

    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(group_type, group) %>%
  transmute(
    Group = paste0(group, " (n=", group_n, ")"),

    `Percentage of individuals with carious lesions` =
      paste0(
        caries_percent,
        "% (",
        caries_affected,
        ")"
      ),

    `Caries Rate (RC)` = sprintf("%.2f", mean_RC)
  )

table_4
```

##Figure 3: Age Distribution####################################################
```{r}
#Figure 3

age_distribution <- stamer.perio.disease %>%
  filter(!is.na(age.cat)) %>%
  mutate(
    age_category = factor(
      age.cat,
      levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
      labels = c(
      "Young adult\n(20–30 years old)",
        "Early middle-aged\n(30–45 years old)",
        "Late middle-aged\n(45–60 years old)",
        "Elderly\n(over 60 years old)"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  count(age_category, name = "n", .drop = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    percent = n / sum(n) * 100
  )

age_distribution


age_distribution_plot <- ggplot(
  age_distribution,
  aes(x = age_category, y = n)
) +
  geom_col(
    fill = "#4472C4",
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = paste0(
        n, " (",
        round(percent), "%)"
      )
    ),
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 4
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Age Category",
    y = "Number of Individuals",
    title = "Age Distribution of the Study Sample"
  ) +
  expand_limits(
    y = max(age_distribution$n) * 1.12
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 30,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

age_distribution_plot

ggsave("Figure_3 Age Distribution.png",
       age_distribution_plot,
       height = 5,
       width = 8,
       dpi = 400)
```

################################################################################


##Predicting Interdental Septum Morphology######################################

  ##first, how well does ADW predict interdental septum morphology?

```{r echo=FALSE}

#fit is a function that describes the relationship between interdental septum and average dental wear; the next chunk contains a visual representation of this relationship but the first panel has a numeric representation
fit <- with(stamer.perio.disease, lm(inter.septum~adw))
summary(fit)
plot(fit)


with(stamer.perio.disease, bptest(fit))

##the relationship between these two variables explains 25.59% of the variation (adjusted r-squared)


```

```{r echo=FALSE}
##this is the model that shows the positive relationship between interdental septum and tooth wear for the entire sample
stamer.perio.disease %>% ggplot(aes(y = inter.septum, x = adw)) +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm', color = 'red') + 
  geom_point(color = 'blue')+
  xlab("Average Dental Wear")+
  ylab("Interdental Septum Morphology")+
  ggtitle("Predicting Interdental Septum Morphology from Average Dental Wear") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
  
```

  ##now using the AIC method to create a multiple linear regression model that explains the most variation

```{r}
##Step 1: Modeling all Relationships
  ##predicting interdental septum morphology from all variables (leaving out caries presence to avoid using the same data twice since I think RC is a better measure)

fit.all.inter.septum <- lm(inter.septum~adw+cej.ac+RC+AMTL+chipping+abcesses+groove+age.cat+sex.cat+time.period, data = stamer.perio.disease)
summary(fit.all.inter.septum)
plot(fit.all.inter.septum)

```

```{r echo=FALSE}
##Step 2: Creating the null model for AIC

lm.null.inter.septum <- lm(inter.septum~1, data = stamer.perio.disease)
summary(lm.null.inter.septum)
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
##Step 3: AIC method forward, building from the null model

AIC.forward.inter.septum <- step(lm.null.inter.septum, 
                    direction='forward', 
                    scope= ~adw+cej.ac+RC+AMTL+chipping+abcesses+groove+age.cat+sex.cat+time.period)
summary(AIC.forward.inter.septum)
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
##Step 4: AIC method backward, taking away from the model with all variables

AIC.backward.inter.septum <- step(fit.all.inter.septum, 
                    direction='backward', 
                    scope= ~adw+cej.ac+RC+AMTL+chipping+abcesses+groove+age.cat+sex.cat+time.period)
summary(AIC.backward.inter.septum)
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
##Step 5: AIC method in both directions

AIC.both.inter.septum <- step(lm.null.inter.septum, 
                    direction='both', 
                    scope= ~adw+cej.ac+RC+AMTL+chipping+abcesses+groove+age.cat+sex.cat+time.period)
summary(AIC.both.inter.septum)

plot(AIC.both.inter.septum)

```
  ##all three AIC methods produced the same answer so I am confident that this model is best

```{r echo=FALSE}
sqrt(vif(AIC.both.inter.septum)) 
```
  ## plotting the model 
```{r}

fit.inter.septum <- lm(formula = inter.septum ~ adw + abcesses + AMTL, data = stamer.perio.disease)
summary(fit.inter.septum )
plot(fit.inter.septum )

##multiple linear regression between interdental septum and ADW, abscesses, and AMTL explains 35.03% of variation (these three variables contribute the most to the severity of inflammation of the gums)
```

```{r}
##Figure 5: Multiple linear regression predicting interdental septum morphology
figure_5 <- stamer.perio.disease %>% ggplot(aes(y = inter.septum, x = fit.inter.septum$fitted.values)) +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm') + 
  geom_point() +
  labs(title="Predicting Interdental Septum Morphology from 
       Average Dental Wear, AMTL, and Abscesses, r=0.3503")+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))+
  xlab("Average Dental Wear, AMTL, and Abscesses")+
  ylab("Interdental Septum Morphology")

##could it be that the few cases of a really high interdental septum score are driven by high AMTL, wear, and abscess scores? Could I show that individuals who bby definition have periodontal disease have a different relationship with these variables than those who do not? 

```
  ##multiple linear regression between interdental septum and ADW, abscesses, and AMTL explains 35.03% of variation (these three variables contribute the most to the severity of inflammation of the gums)

#CEJ-AC distance################################################################


  ##now using the AIC method to create a multiple linear regression model that explains the most variation

```{r}
##Step 1: Modeling all Relationships
  ##predicting eCEJ-AC distance from all variables (leaving out caries presence to avoid using the same data twice since I think RC is a better measure)

fit.all.CEJ.AC <- lm(cej.ac~adw+inter.septum+RC+AMTL+chipping+abcesses+groove+age.cat+sex.cat+time.period, data = stamer.perio.disease)
summary(fit.all.CEJ.AC)
plot(fit.all.CEJ.AC)

```

```{r echo=FALSE}
##Step 2: Creating the null model for AIC

lm.null.CEJ.AC <- lm(cej.ac~1, data = stamer.perio.disease)
summary(lm.null.CEJ.AC)
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
##Step 3: AIC method forward, building from the null model

AIC.forward.CEJ.AC <- step(lm.null.CEJ.AC, 
                    direction='forward', 
                    scope= ~adw+inter.septum+RC+AMTL+chipping+abcesses+groove+age.cat+sex.cat+time.period)
summary(AIC.forward.CEJ.AC)
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
##Step 4: AIC method backward, taking away from the model with all variables

AIC.backward.CEJ.AC <- step(fit.all.CEJ.AC, 
                    direction='backward', 
                    scope= ~adw+inter.septum+RC+AMTL+chipping+abcesses+groove+age.cat+sex.cat+time.period)
summary(AIC.backward.CEJ.AC)
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
##Step 5: AIC method in both directions

AIC.both.CEJ.AC <- step(lm.null.CEJ.AC, 
                    direction='both', 
                    scope= ~adw+inter.septum+RC+AMTL+chipping+abcesses+groove+age.cat+sex.cat+time.period)
summary(AIC.both.CEJ.AC)

plot(AIC.both.CEJ.AC)

```
##all three AIC methods produced the same answer so I am confident that this model is best

```{r echo=FALSE}
sqrt(vif(AIC.both.CEJ.AC)) 
```
## plotting the model 
```{r}

fit.CEJ.AC <- lm(formula = cej.ac ~ AMTL + adw + sex.cat + chipping, data = stamer.perio.disease)
summary(fit.CEJ.AC)
plot(fit.CEJ.AC)

##multiple linear regression between CEJ-AC distance and AMTL, ADW, and sex explains 31.32% of variation (these three variables contribute the most to the resorption of the alveolar bone)
```

```{r}
fit.all.inter.time.period <- lm(time.period~inter.septum+adw+cej.ac+RC+AMTL+chipping+abcesses+groove+age.cat+sex.cat, data = stamer.perio.disease)
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
                    direction='both',
```

#Chi Squared Tests of Significance##############################################
```{r}
statistical_test_data <- stamer.perio.disease %>%
  mutate(
    sex = factor(
      sex.cat,
      levels = c(1, 2),
      labels = c("Male", "Female")
    ),

    septum_y_n = factor(
      inter.septum >= 3,
      levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
      labels = c("Absent", "Present")
    ),

    cej_y_n = factor(
      cej.ac >= 2,
      levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
      labels = c("Absent", "Present")
    ),

    caries_present = factor(
      caries == 2,
      levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
      labels = c("Absent", "Present")
    ),

    amtl_present = factor(
      AMTL > 0,
      levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
      labels = c("Absent", "Present")
    )
  )
#is the difference in periodontal disease rates significant between the two measures?
perio.difference <- with(
  statistical_test_data ,
  table(
    CEJ_AC = cej_y_n,
    Interdental_septum = septum_y_n
  )
)
perio.difference
addmargins(perio.difference)

perio.difference.test <- mcnemar.test(perio.difference)
perio.difference.test

#is the interdental septum different based on sex
inter.sex <- with(
  statistical_test_data,
  table(
    Sex = sex,
    Interdental_septum = septum_y_n
  )
)

inter.sex
addmargins(inter.sex)

inter.sex.test <- chisq.test(inter.sex)

inter.sex.test

#is CEJ_AC difference based on sex
cej.sex <- with(
  statistical_test_data,
  table(
    Sex = sex,
    CEJ_AC = cej_y_n
  )
)

cej.sex
addmargins(cej.sex)

cej.sex.test <- chisq.test(cej.sex)

cej.sex.test


#caries/sex
caries.sex <- with(
  statistical_test_data,
  table(
    Sex = sex,
    Caries = caries_present
  )
)

caries.sex
addmargins(caries.sex)

caries.sex.test <- chisq.test(caries.sex)

caries.sex.test

#AMTL/sex
amtl.sex <- with(
  statistical_test_data,
  table(
    Sex = sex,
    AMTL = amtl_present
  )
)

amtl.sex
addmargins(amtl.sex)

amtl.sex.test <- chisq.test(amtl.sex)

amtl.sex.test

#wear/sex
wear.sex.test <- wilcox.test(
  adw ~ sex,
  data = statistical_test_data,
  exact = FALSE
)

wear.sex.test

#chipping/sex
chipping.sex.test <- wilcox.test(
  chipping ~ sex,
  data = statistical_test_data,
  exact = FALSE
)

chipping.sex.test

statistical_test_data %>%
  group_by(sex) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(chipping)),
    mean = mean(chipping, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(chipping, na.rm = TRUE),
    IQR = IQR(chipping, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

#abscesses/sex
abscesses.sex.test <- wilcox.test(
  abcesses ~ sex,
  data = statistical_test_data,
  exact = FALSE
)

abscesses.sex.test


#Bonferroni correction
p_values <- c(
  Caries = caries.sex.test$p.value,
  AMTL = amtl.sex.test$p.value,
  Dental_wear = wear.sex.test$p.value,
  Chipping = chipping.sex.test$p.value,
  Abscesses = abscesses.sex.test$p.value
)

adjusted_results <- data.frame(
  Test = names(p_values),
  Raw_p = unname(p_values),
  Holm_p = unname(
    p.adjust(p_values, method = "holm")
  )
)

adjusted_results
```
